note: Iron Rock bolt-on, frame-mounted; sliders that bolt only to the body are not worth buying.
OME 3-inch kit with Nitrocharger shocks, enough for 33s. Skip the spacer kits if 33s are the plan.
Rough Country adjustable bar, the guide's budget pick; it re-centers the axle after a lift.
Five 15x8 Pro Comp steel wheels at $75 each with 3.75 inches of backspacing, so the 33s clear the control arms.
Five 33x10.50R15 all-terrains; 3.73 gears pull 33s but the 3.07s in many automatics do not.
Tom Wood's SYE plus CV rear driveshaft stops the highway vibration above 2.5 inches of lift. It does not fit a Rubicon's transfer case.
Powertrax lunchbox on the Dana 35, a light-foot fix at 33s. Skip on a Rubicon, which has a factory rear locker.
Skid Row engine and transmission skid; the TJ already has factory transfer case and tank skids, so skip a heavy-duty t-case skid.
Smittybilt XRC stubby with a winch plate; the guide says most TJs never outgrow the $450 tier.
Iron Rock with a swing-out carrier, since the factory tailgate hinges fatigue under a spare past a 32.
Frame-mount recovery points; the factory front hooks are rated, so this is for a TJ that lost them or needs a rear point.
Smittybilt X20 Gen2 at 9,500 pounds, with synthetic rope from the factory.
RockJock Currectlync, a straight solid bar for 33s on rocks; over 4 inches of lift it needs a dropped pitman arm.
Synergy chromoly drag link for 33s to 35s; on the TJ's Y-link steering it carries both front wheels.
Ford 8.8 swap for the Dana 35, the low end of the guide's $1,200 to $2,200 all-in. A Rubicon already has a Dana 44 rear.
Iron Rock 4.5-inch bolt-on long arm, in the 4 to 5 inches the 35-inch guide calls for.
Dana 30 chromoly front shafts, the minimum the 35-inch guide asks for before 35s.
Both axles together: 4.88 for 35s on a manual, and the fitment guide calls for 5.13 on an automatic.
Five 35x12.50R15s at about $280 each; plan fender trimming, and check the speedometer after the regear.
